title: Introducing Reverend Gensel's Jazz Vespers
summary: Green describes Reverend Gensel as the jazz priest of the Jazz Vespers.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did she have anything to do with you dancing at the Jazz Vespers?
Tell me a little bit about that.

Well, she told me to always go to where the parotials (sic) were. Once you get a new doing and rebaptized, you know, that's like -- that's like joining the meeting Christ all over again, you see. And it's really good for anyone. It's like food, you know, to the passions, you see.
Can you tell me a little bit about the Jazz Vespers with Reverend John Ginzo?
Oh, that's new. That's so transparent.
Well, that's the greatest. I think that's the greatest -- what they call it -- I call it -- I say medicine, you know. Because it's a re-awakening of what God is to his own image, you see.
Well, what does Reverend Ginzo do?

Well, he's -- I would say he was in -- he's some kind of -- he's a great author, you see. He's a great authority of anyone's compassion, you know. I mean to the -- you know, the humane personages that's in people's personalities, you see.
What I really mean to say is what has he done for jazz and for tap dancing.

Well, he has -- he's relocated jazz. They should really donate a broadcasting station to this man because -- this reverend, you see, because I think he's the originality of what they call the jazz priest, you see. But only he's a reverend, you see. So, there's a difference in the degrees, see. I think the reverend is kind of a little further on the bone than the priests, you know. He's more like an elder, you see. And like classes, like student bodies, you know, that's -- that wants to remain studious, you know, or they wants to branch out, you know.
